Theme

Latin word

ipse

pronoun, intensive: genitive ipsīus, dative ipsī

himself (for emphasis: he himself, in person, of his own accord); itself (for emphasis: the thing itself, of its own accord); the very, just, exactly; myself (for emphasis: I myself, in person); oneself (for emphasis); self, one’s very self (with the reflexive: sē ipsum, tē ipsum); yourself (for emphasis: you yourself)

In this lexicon

  • himself

    the recommended word · classical · Publ. Q 69: Quī sē ipse laudat, citō dērīsōrem invenit.; Liv. 22.2.10: ipse Hannibal

  • itself

    the recommended word · classical · Col. 12.2.6: ipse vacuus locus admonet; Plin. NH 18.104: ex ipsā farīnā

  • just

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Fam. 7.23.4: eā ipsā hōrā (Lewis & Short); Cic. Att. 3.21: trīgintā diēs erant ipsī, it was just thirty days (Lewis & Short)

  • myself

    the recommended word · classical · Plin. NH 8.6: ipse ego haec scrīpsī; Cic. Amic. 10: mē ipse cōnsōlor (Lewis & Short, s.v. ipse, Lael. 3.10)

  • oneself

    also used · classical

  • self

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Fin. 1.67: nisi aequē amīcōs et nōsmet ipsōs dīligāmus (Lewis & Short); Hor. Ep. 1.2.33: ut tē ipsum servēs

  • yourself

    the recommended word · classical · Hor. Ep. 1.2.33: ut tē ipsum servēs; Cic. Fam. 9.14.8: fac ut dīligentissimē tē ipsum custōdiās (Lewis & Short, s.v. ipse)

    classical

Examples

  • Quī sē ipse laudat, citō dērīsōrem invenit.

    Whoever praises himself soon finds someone to laugh at him.Publ. Q 69

  • sī quid forte abest, ipse vacuus locus admonet, ut, quod deest, requīrātur
